## Dataset

**Source:** Synthetic support-ticket dataset generated by `task1_dataset.py`
(template-based, fixed random seed 42). It is not real customer data, so it is
safe to share, and it can be regenerated exactly by re-running the script.

**Columns:** `text` (ticket message), `category` (Billing / Technical / Account / Shipping),
`priority` (High / Medium / Low).

**Cleaning:** lowercase, trim, collapse repeated spaces, drop empty rows and exact
duplicates (40 duplicates removed). Final size: **680 tickets**.

**Realism notes:** about 20% of tickets use an urgency phrase that does not match their
priority, and about 6% mention two topics. This adds label noise and confusing cases so
the models are not tested on an unrealistically easy dataset.

### Class balance

| Category | Tickets | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Technical | 229 | 33.7% |
| Billing | 194 | 28.5% |
| Account | 160 | 23.5% |
| Shipping | 97 | 14.3% |

| Priority | Tickets | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Medium | 308 | 45.3% |
| High | 186 | 27.4% |
| Low | 186 | 27.4% |

### Split (stratified on category + priority, seed 42)

| Split | Rows |
|---|---|
| Train (70%) | 476 |
| Validation (15%) | 102 |
| Test (15%) | 102 |

Files: `data/train.csv`, `data/val.csv`, `data/test.csv` (same columns as above).

## Baseline (TF-IDF + Logistic Regression)
- Tuned ngram_range and C with 5-fold CV (macro F1).
- Validation: Category accuracy __, macro F1 __ | Priority accuracy __, macro F1 __
- Category is near perfect because synthetic tickets use clear keywords. Priority is harder because urgency wording is noisy.
- Bonus: character n-grams did not help (or helped by __), see results/baseline_char_ngram_comparison.csv
- Model files: models/baseline_category.joblib, models/baseline_priority.joblib
